question: Methotrexate is the first-line disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drug (DMARD) for children with JIA who fail to respond adequately to NSAIDs, and it requires monitoring for hepatotoxicity.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Methotrexate is well established as the first-line DMARD in JIA across most subtypes. It is given once weekly (NOT daily) with concomitant folic acid. Hepatotoxicity is a recognised adverse effect requiring regular liver function monitoring.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Methotrexate (10-15 mg/m² once weekly, oral or subcutaneous) is the cornerstone DMARD for JIA when NSAIDs are insufficient. Folic acid supplementation is co-prescribed to reduce mucosal and haematological side effects, and liver function tests must be monitored regularly given the risk of hepatotoxicity.
